The maternal creatine homeostasis is indeed altered during gestation in mice, specifically undergoing changes that allow for increased creatine synthesis and reduced creatine excretion. This physiological adjustment is crucial to meet the additional demands placed on maternal tissues and the developing fetus during pregnancy.

This adaptation is a vital metabolic response to support the growing offspring, enabling them to develop properly under the heightened energy needs of fetal growth and development. By modifying creatine levels, mice pregnant with spiny mice are better equipped to provide for their offspring's high-energy requirements throughout gestation.
